For mixed sources, normalize coordinates and energy values before combining them. A unit label does not make values compatible. The Data.from_file CP2K adapter does not expose arbitrary time units; use cremer_pople_trajectory for explicit nonuniform times and another unit label.

docs.title: Cremer–Pople coordinates
docs.text:
For an ordered ring with positions indexed by j=0,...,N-1, coordinates are centered at the ring centroid. The mean-plane normal is the normalized cross product R_sine × R_cosine. Heights z_j are projections onto that normal. The second-mode components follow

q2 * cos(phi) =  sqrt(2/N) * sum_j(z[j] * cos(4*pi*j/N))
q2 * sin(phi) = -sqrt(2/N) * sum_j(z[j] * sin(4*pi*j/N))

For six-membered rings,

q3 = sum_j((-1)**j * z[j]) / sqrt(6)
Q = sqrt(q2**2 + q3**2)
theta = atan2(q2, q3)

Five-membered rings have Q=q2 and no q3 or theta. Phi is normalized to [0, 360) or [0, 2π); theta to [0, 180] or [0, π]. Starting-atom changes, traversal reversals, and reflections alter angular conventions. Proper rigid rotations and translations do not.

Undefined angles are represented by NaN: phi for a planar ring or pure chair, theta for a planar ring. Zero amplitude is different from an undefined mean plane: collapsed or collinear coordinates can make the plane degenerate and raise ValueError.

docs.title: Canonical pucker names are positional
docs.text:
Six-membered classification uses 38 CarPpy reference vectors of three transformed diagonal dihedrals. Its carppy_theta is a three-component vector, not the scalar CP polar theta. Its reference distance is Euclidean distance in that three-angle space, in degrees.

For the standard oxygen-first six-membered order, labels use 1–5 for the carbon positions after O and 6 for O. For an aldopyranose these coincide with C1–C5. For a ketose, they describe ring positions rather than chemical carbon numbering. The sphere plot writes O instead of 6 in its ideal-position annotations.

Five-membered labels use positions 0–4 in supplied ring order and nearest envelope/twist phase. Their distance is the shortest wrapped phase difference in degrees. Do not compare the five- and six-membered distances as if they were the same metric.

planar indicates amplitude below the configured tolerance. unassigned means the closest reference exceeded max_distance; nearest_label and the nearest family remain available. These are shape classifications, not energy estimates, proof of stability, or population measurements.

See Puckering for synthetic examples that reproduce known coordinates and demonstrate rejection tolerances.

docs.title: Torsion definitions
docs.text:
StateEditor.get_dihedral, four-atom measure/measure_internal calls, and glycan torsions use the same signed convention. For coordinates a, b, c, d, let u be the unit vector from b toward c, and project the two terminal vectors onto the plane perpendicular to u:

u = (c - b) / norm(c - b)
v = (a - b) - dot(a - b, u) * u
w = (d - c) - dot(d - c, u) * u
dihedral = atan2(dot(cross(u, v), w), dot(v, w))

Convert the result to degrees for StateEditor; its range is [-180, 180]. Positive angles follow a right-handed rotation from v toward w about u. For a=(0,1,0), b=(0,0,0), c=(1,0,0), and d=(1,0,1), the result is +90°. Reflecting all z coordinates changes it to −90°; a rigid translation or proper rotation preserves it. Reversing the entire four-atom order also preserves the angle. Exact 0° and ±180° are valid; coincident central atoms or collinear triples make a torsion undefined and raise ValueError.

The legacy StateEditor sign has been corrected to this convention, including a translation-dependent sign bug. Glycan and ring-analysis conventions are unchanged. For saved legacy measurements, recompute from coordinates rather than assuming every value needs only a sign flip. The interactive geometry tutorial demonstrates the corrected sign and translation invariance.

Glycosidic phi is donor ring O–anomeric C–linking O–acceptor C. Psi continues through the preceding acceptor backbone carbon, using its ring O for an anomeric acceptor. Terminal-carbon glycosidic omega is linking O–terminal C–ring C–ring O. Hydroxymethyl backbone omega lists those four atoms in the reverse order.

Always compare the reported atom_indices quadruplets as well as angle names. “Phi,” “psi,” and “omega” do not by themselves establish a universal definition across programs. Backbone omega is None for missing or ambiguous terminal oxygens; a glycosidic omega key is absent when that linkage has no corresponding terminal-carbon torsion.

docs.title: Periodic boundaries and trajectories
docs.text:
Puckering, RMSD, and glycan torsion routines do not apply periodic-boundary corrections. Supply whole, unwrapped molecules or rings. Atoms split across a cell boundary may look far apart, break bond detection, or generate meaningless geometrical values even if all entries are finite.

Trajectory assignments are fixed at the reference/first frame. They are appropriate for a consistent atom ordering and topology, not a reactive trajectory that changes connectivity. Coordinate generators are consumed once; results retain the numeric analysis rows but not every input geometry. Space.from_xyz instead loads every coordinate frame into memory.

Glycan.from_file uses the last XYZ/CP2K frame. Space.from_xyz loads all frames. Automatic trajectory detection uses the first frame. Choose the entry point deliberately when a file contains more than one geometry.

docs.title: Counts and free energy on the sphere
docs.text:
Plot.cremer_pople_sphere pools one count per valid row into (phi, theta) angular bins. The displayed map has longitude 180° − phi and latitude 90° − theta. Histograms are stored in (latitude, longitude) order; stored edges are radians. Five-membered rings cannot use this projection.

Pure chairs contribute to a pole using arbitrary phase 180°; planar and other undefined-angle frames are omitted. Each valid frame receives equal weight, regardless of time spacing, frame order, or dataset length. Longer datasets therefore contribute more counts when pooled.

The default map computes ΔG = −R T ln(N/Nmax) using R=8.314 J/(mol K). Empty bins are masked, and the most populated bin is zero. This is free energy per angular cell, without spherical-area correction or reweighting. Interpolated drawing grids affect only rendering; conformer_counts and free_energy keep the original bin resolution.

A reference library or biased/unequally sampled collection does not automatically represent equilibrium populations. Use quantity="counts" for a descriptive view of such data. See Trajectories for plotting and export examples.

docs.title: RMSD and clustering
docs.text:
Aligned RMSD uses translation removal and a proper Kabsch rotation. It does not allow reflections or symmetry-based atom permutations. The fit and distance use the same atom selection. Single-pair rmsd defaults to all atoms; pairwise matrices and clustering default to heavy atoms.

Clustering uses SciPy hierarchical linkage on condensed RMSD distances. All cluster indices refer back to original inputs; energy-excluded labels are -1. With complete finite energies, representatives minimize the chosen energy attribute. Otherwise they minimize summed within-cluster RMSD (medoids). energy=None explicitly selects medoids.

The complete distance matrix is quadratic in the number of inputs and is calculated before energy filtering. Duplicate removal uses complete linkage, ensuring every pair in a duplicate group is within the threshold. Neither clustering nor duplicate removal changes coordinates or reorders the source Space.

docs.title: Reference-data provenance
docs.text:
The four bundled carbohydrate fixtures come from the CarPpy benchmark set at commit 4589b228cf8772b0f2bd6ccae8bb2f41ad1e7d70. The coordinates and atom order are retained; XYZ comment lines record source paths. glucose_puckers.xyz concatenates 38 reference conformations in source-path order and is not a molecular dynamics trajectory.

The repository's tests/data/README.md documents upstream paths and algorithm provenance. The adaptation adds matmalib object integration, fixed trajectory assignments, ambiguity checks, supported five-membered phase classification, medoid selection, and complete-linkage duplicate removal. CarPpy is not required at runtime. Source tests verify reference atom assignments, all 38 canonical labels, stereochemistry, torsions, cluster behavior, and SNFG drawing geometry.

docs.title: Core API behavior and implementation notes
docs.text: This page complements the generated API reference with behavior that is easy to miss in signatures. Every public class and method in core.py, util.py, calc.py, and elements.py is included below. The walkthroughs are molecules and geometry, I/O, and ensembles.

docs.title: Units, indexing, and mutable data
docs.text:
• Coordinates have no attached unit. The examples and default bond cutoffs assume angstroms; distance and RMSD results retain the input units.
  • Legacy internal-coordinate angles use degrees. Space.diff assumes hartree input and always returns kcal/mol using 627.5095.
  • Use zero-based positions, with Atom.id == position, in legacy connectivity and distance/angle editing code. Dihedral measurements/edits and newer glycan and conformer APIs use atom-list positions independently of Atom.id.
  • State and Data accept arbitrary keyword attributes. They do not validate or infer all required metadata.
  • Atoms, fragment memberships, and state collections are generally shared by reference. Use copy.deepcopy when an independent geometry is required.

docs.title: StateEditor
docs.text:
StateEditor(state) retains the supplied state; edits mutate it. Static measurement methods accept all Atom objects, or all Python integer positions with state=...; get_dihedral additionally accepts NumPy integer positions. Avoid collinear triples, coincident atoms, and mixed selections.

Public method Return / mutation get_distance(atom_list, state=None) Euclidean distance, expected length 2. get_angle(atom_list, state=None) (degrees, cross_product_axis), expected length 3; axis is unnormalized. get_dihedral(atom_list, state=None, ax=False) Signed degrees in [-180, 180], using the shared, translation-invariant atan2 convention. Requires exactly four finite three-component coordinates; negative/out-of-range positions, coincident central atoms, and collinear triples raise ValueError. With ax=True, returns (degrees, cross_product_axis); the compatibility axis is unnormalized and can be zero for planar geometry. measure(atom_list, state=None) Dispatches by selection length 2/3/4; other lengths return None. adjacent_atoms(conn_mat, at) NumPy array of nonzero neighbor positions in row at. connect_atoms(state, at1, at2) Sets both matrix entries to one; does not update the graph. disconnect_atoms(state, at1, at2) Sets both matrix entries to zero; does not update the graph. determine_carried_atoms(state, atom_list) Temporarily removes a bond and returns the Atom objects in the second atom's connected component, normally restoring the bond. If the matrix stays connected, returns None after printing and currently leaves that bond removed. set_distance(atom_list, new_distance) Requires two Python integer positions; translates the carried component. New distance uses input units. Returns None. set_angle(atom_list, new_ang) Requires three Python integer positions; rotates the third atom's component around the middle atom, in degrees. Returns None. set_dihedral(atom_list, new_dih, incr=False, axis_pos="bond", threshold=0.1) Requires four distinct Python or NumPy integer positions within the state. Rotation requires a finite symmetric conn_mat indexed by atom position and containing the selected bond. With incr=True, adds the requested angle. "bond" rotates the third atom's component about the central bond, preserving connectivity and rejecting cyclic bonds. "term" uses a parallel axis through the last atom and rotates atoms beyond it, leaving the selected quartet unchanged. Targets/increments wrap modulo 360°; finite targets and a finite, nonnegative tolerance are required. Returns None.

The setters only manipulate geometry; there is no relaxation, collision checking, ring-closure constraint, or automatic topology update. set_dihedral uses the central-bond direction for a stable rotation axis, supports exact 0° and ±180° targets, and rejects unsupported axis_pos values. Its threshold only skips changes at or below the angular tolerance; it does not alter the target to avoid planar geometry. The distance/angle setters and direct determine_carried_atoms calls retain the legacy connectivity limitations listed above. Keep a copy and remeasure outputs.

Dihedral compatibility: the sign of get_dihedral and its measure/measure_internal wrappers has been corrected to match the existing glycan torsion convention. The legacy translation-dependent sign error and small offsets at 0°/±180° are also fixed. Saved legacy results should be recomputed from coordinates, and absolute/incremental targets for set_dihedral now follow the corrected sign. Glycan torsions and ring calculations retain their existing convention. See the formula and worked example.

docs.title: StateBuilder
docs.text:
StateBuilder(path, software) stores its inputs. Parser methods mutate the builder; build() constructs a new State from all builder attributes, computes legacy connectivity, and splits components.

Public method Behavior element_symbol(A) Same 1–118 atomic-number mapping as State.element_symbol. gaussian() Parses selected Gaussian route types, geometry, available energy/thermal fields, vibrational data, and lower-triangular NMR couplings. Mutates builder attributes and returns None. Format-sensitive; not every Gaussian output layout is supported. cp2k_geom() Reads the last NAtoms coordinate lines from an XYZ trajectory. Atom IDs are currently unset because indices are passed positionally as valence. Prefer Space.from_xyz. orca() Incomplete optimization/energy-only parser. An energy match may return the builder, but it does not supply the geometry required by build; the optimization branch has path and variable errors. build() Dispatches "cp2k", "gaussian", "orca"; unknown software raises ValueError. Returns a State only if parsing, connectivity, and splitting succeed.

docs.title: DataBuilder
docs.text:
DataBuilder(path, software, **kwargs) retains every keyword as an attribute. Methods populate .data and metadata on the builder; build() returns a Data with a shallow copy of those attributes.

Public method Behavior csv(skiprows=0, dtype=float, delimiter=",") Calls np.loadtxt; attributes supplied to the builder override these method defaults/arguments. Returns None. cp2k_md(colvar=None, timestep=None) For XYZ, computes a legacy coordinate or dispatches structured Cremer–Pople analysis. Explicit non-None method arguments override builder colvar/timestep. For .metadynLog, reads the numeric table unchanged. Sets time_unit="fs". Returns None. gromacs() Parses a limited XVG numeric table/header or a square uppercase-key XPM matrix. Values are not converted. Returns None. build() Dispatches "cp2k", "gromacs", "csv"; unknown software raises ValueError. Returns Data.

CP2K coordinate extraction requires colvar and timestep, except .metadynLog table loading. Two/four atom selections produce distance/dihedral data; three-atom tuples currently fail numeric array assembly. XYZ selections follow file order, not arbitrary colvar order. The observable="cremer_pople" route requires timestep, accepts rings, degrees, conn_mat, distXX, distXH, and classify, and uses the validated trajectory implementation. Other CP2K/GROMACS suffixes may yield a container with no data attribute because those parser branches do not reject unknown file formats.

docs.title: InputBuilder
docs.text:
InputBuilder(path=None, theory=None, software="gaussian", space=None) only stores settings. build(space, theory, software, path, names=None) sets all these again plus names, then invokes a writer. For predictable behavior call build; gaussian() reads self.names, which the constructor does not initialize.

Public method Behavior element_number(A) Case-sensitive element symbol to integer atomic number, 1–118; unknown symbols raise KeyError. gaussian() Expects space.states. Creates <path>/<id>/input.com, rounds coordinates to three decimals, mutates the dispersion setting, and overwrites existing files. Non-None names currently raises an error; set state IDs directly. xyz() Expects an iterable of states, such as space.states. Creates <path>/<id>/geometry.xyz with three-decimal coordinates; no trajectory concatenation. fhiaims() Legacy incomplete writer with a site-specific basis directory, absolute geometry output path, and Atom/string formatting error. Do not rely on it to produce valid FHI-aims inputs. build(space, theory, software, path, names=None) Dispatches "gaussian", "xyz", "fhiaims"; unknown values silently do nothing. Returns None.

The output parent directory must already exist. Use unique directory-safe state.id values and review generated input before submitting it to external software. Required Gaussian theory keys are disp, nprocs, mem, method, basis_set, jobtype, charge, and multiplicity; optional keys are other_options and extra. See the complete input generation example.

docs.title: Element mappings
docs.text:
matmalib.elements contains the standard symbols for elements 1 through 118. ELEMENT_SYMBOLS has string atomic-number keys; ELEMENT_NUMBERS has case-sensitive symbol keys and integer values. These are ordinary dictionaries, not a periodic-table database: masses, isotopes, radii, and valences are not supplied.

from matmalib import State, StateBuilder
from matmalib.calc import InputBuilder
from matmalib.elements import ELEMENT_SYMBOLS, ELEMENT_NUMBERS

print("Elements:", len(ELEMENT_SYMBOLS))
for number in (1, 6, 8, 26, 79, 118):
    symbol = ELEMENT_SYMBOLS[str(number)]
    print(number, symbol, ELEMENT_NUMBERS[symbol])

print(State.element_symbol(26))
print(StateBuilder.element_symbol("79"))
print(InputBuilder.element_number("Og"))

The wrappers convert numeric inputs to strings before lookup, so State.element_symbol(6) and State.element_symbol("6") both return "C". 6.0, zero, missing elements, and wrong symbol case are not normalized and raise KeyError. Try changing: look up another integer from 1 through 118, then compare direct dictionary lookup with the wrappers.

docs.title: Sample data and attribution
docs.text:
The live examples use the repository's small, public test fixtures. Each build copies them directly from tests/data; the runner sees the same content at data/....

Download Purpose glucose.xyz A glucose geometry for recognition, numbering, and measurement glycan.xyz A multi-residue carbohydrate for linkage analysis glucose_puckers.xyz The 38-reference glucose conformer ensemble fucosylated_trisaccharide.xyz A branched three-residue glycan for SNFG and torsions

These are demonstration and regression fixtures, not an equilibrium molecular-dynamics trajectory. Population maps of their conformers illustrate an algorithm; they do not establish physical free energies. Tutorials explicitly label synthetic trajectories and numerical data.

docs.title: Scientific provenance
docs.text:
Carbohydrate detection, atom numbering, and six-membered canonical pucker classification adapt work from CarPpy. The detailed fixture provenance, upstream commit, adaptation scope, and benchmark construction are recorded in the data README.

Cremer–Pople coordinates follow Cremer and Pople, JACS (1975). Glycan symbol conventions follow the Symbol Nomenclature for Glycans (SNFG). The library's exact phase, ordering, angle, and classification conventions are described in Units and conventions.

The website uses Material for MkDocs, mkdocstrings, and Pyodide. Browser calculations use NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib, NetworkX, colormaps, and py3Dmol.
